sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Paʼa language' (accessed 2026-09-17), phonology section sourced to Skinner 1979.
sources.note: Gives consonants, five vowels short/long, diphthongs ei/au, and 'Pa'a also has four tones; high, mid, low, and falling.' No statement about stress.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena Publications.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' (p. 5) covers all North Bauchi languages incl. Pa'a: 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' No mention of stress or accent anywhere (grep of full text).
